about: A Zork-like start: a white house, a kitchen, a living room with a trapdoor to a cellar, and a troll. Past the troll, the cavern is unfinished, with "back soon" notes in place of rooms.

done.why: Every exit past the Troll Room is blocked by a joke note, so there was nothing further to pursue.

moments.note: The window, the lantern, the rug and the trapdoor all worked as expected.
The troll was in the room right at the stairs' foot and died to a single sword hit.
The east exit was an unfinished-passage note, not a room.
The south crawlway and the west hole also dead-end, so the cavern has nowhere to go.
The pick mentioned in the note can't be taken or seen.

wished: Somewhere to go past the troll
To take the pick and dig

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. Someone has left a pick leaning against the rock, and a note: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: A wry way of saying the world stops here.

fun.why: The opening was a pleasant, familiar run, then it hit walls.

engagement.why: I had a clear goal until the cavern ended.

difficulty.why: Everything worked at once and the troll fell in one blow.

interestingness.why: A familiar setting with a charming unfinished edge.

prose.why: The prose is crisp and recognisably Zork.
